implemented_contracts: feature-gated bundled SQLite Registry with WAL, FULL synchronous writes, migrations, private permissions, and fail-closed validation
server-generated Job and Attempt identities with atomic principal and client-request idempotency
atomic global and profile concurrency reservations with held-orphaned capacity semantics
append-only Job events, immutable terminal resolution, Artifact lineage, and bounded Job listing
immutable Attempt bundles and a persisted at-most-once dispatch boundary before systemd launch
Runner launch identity binding across PID namespace, host MainPID, InvocationID, cgroup, boot ID, and process start identity
atomic terminal and intent-first cancellation transactions with startup and targeted reconciliation
independent M6 MCP adapter projecting SQLite Job identity as Native MCP Task identity
real 2/4/8 concurrency, eight systemd recovery journeys, bounded model-in-the-loop evaluation, and M5-to-M6 Shadow comparison
independent evidence recomputation and tamper rejection
evidence: Eight M6 Dogfood journeys succeeded with 39 model-facing calls, 19817 context bytes, one repair round, zero fallback, disconnect recovery, cancellation cleanup, and idempotent replay. Real 2/4/8 Job batches preserved unique identities, rejected the final excess request with CONCURRENCY_LIMIT, and released all 14 reservations. Eight systemd recovery journeys passed, including ten consecutive fast failures without a lost misclassification. Registry p95 values were 20.30 ms admission, 0.97 ms replay, 0.86 ms status, 5.11 ms list-100, and 21.15 ms terminal. Twelve M5-versus-M6 Shadow pairs were semantically equivalent; overall medians were M5 509 ms and 1687 context bytes versus M6 603 ms and 1754 context bytes with equal calls and HTTP requests.
verification_result: M6 is eligible for continued bounded local transactional Dogfood only. The evidence does not authorize production routing, remote exposure, credentials, deployment, push, merge, network access, or external side effects.
degraded_reasons: The M6 Registry backend was 18.5 percent slower than the M5 file backend in the bounded twelve-pair Shadow matrix.
M6 returned about 4 percent more Context than M5 in the bounded Shadow matrix.
Only one bounded model-in-the-loop journey was executed; broad autonomous planning quality remains unproven.
The recovery matrix reconstructs Core and injects systemd failures but does not perform an actual WSL reboot.
Execution still lacks a dedicated non-privileged Worker identity.
Retention, quota, garbage collection, operational remediation for held-orphaned capacity, and remote authentication remain absent.
Repository document governance retains the exact three pre-existing violations from the M6 design base.
remaining_debt: Move execution to a dedicated non-privileged Worker before expanding authority or external capabilities.
Add actual WSL reboot recovery, startup reconciliation evidence across boot changes, and operator remediation for orphaned Attempts.
Implement retention, quota, garbage collection, Registry backup and recovery, and bounded evidence compaction.
Strengthen machine-enforced capability policy beyond the current local repository, executable-root, sandbox, and transport boundaries.
Expand model-driven evaluation to longer repair loops, Rust build failures, concurrent planning, and adversarial tool selection.
Keep Cloudflare, remote MCP, credentials, deployment, push, merge, network access, and external side effects in separate authority stages.

authorization.rationale: M6 uses an independent localhost-only experimental MCP adapter and explicitly excludes production routing and external side effects.

next_bounded_action: Design the next stage around a dedicated non-privileged Worker and lifecycle governance while continuing M6 only as bounded local transactional Dogfood evidence.
